attacks.claim: Offline expiry only catches a device clock set earlier than the download time. A clock set back to any time between download and valid_until shows a forecast that has already expired, which violates 'never shows an expired rating in color, including in offline maps'. The QA check tests only the one direction.
attacks.evidence: "if the device clock reads earlier than that, the stored forecast is treated as expired" / QA: "Device clock moved earlier than offline download time | Pass"

attacks.claim: The zone color is an app-derived aggregate (max of three bands), not the rating as issued. The agreement forbids altering ratings, and the artifact says the app never derives ratings itself.
attacks.evidence: "The zone color uses the highest of the three" vs "We show the rating exactly as issued" and "We never interpolate, smooth, or forecast ratings ourselves"

attacks.claim: The bbox of visible tiles sent to an unauthenticated endpoint, with origin IP logs, reveals approximate user location and is linkable over time. The claim that location is not sent is true only for GPS; viewport bbox plus IP is still location data. Log retention is not specified.
attacks.evidence: "The app requests forecasts by zone id for the visible map tiles" / "GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…" / "device location is not sent" / ABSENT: origin log retention and IP handling

attacks.claim: CDN TTL and cache invalidation are not stated. A center revision or retraction before valid_until may not reach clients until the CDN entry expires, so the 10-min poll does not bound how long a superseded rating is served as current.
attacks.evidence: "Our backend polls WADE every 10 min and serves zone geometry + ratings from our CDN." / ABSENT: CDN TTL, purge-on-revision, max staleness

attacks.claim: bbox is unbounded, and at 8% CDN miss the origin sees about 144k requests/day. A 10-100x load or large-bbox queries can saturate the 6-instance origin cap and produce 5xx before the 1% alert fires. Cost estimates assume the projected traffic shape.
attacks.evidence: "Projected 1.8M zone requests/day at 92% CDN hit rate" / "origin autoscaling capped at 6 instances" / ABSENT: bbox size limit

attacks.claim: Storing forecasts for offline use goes beyond the display permission quoted. The artifact does not cite the agreement's position on offline caching or retention, nor confirm the legal review covered it.
attacks.evidence: "display in our app is permitted" / "the current forecast for those zones is stored with it" / ABSENT: agreement clause on offline storage

attacks.claim: Attribution appears only in the tap card. The map layer itself shows ratings with no center attribution, which may not meet the attribution requirement.
attacks.evidence: "we must attribute and link to the issuing center" / "Tapping a zone opens a summary card"

attacks.claim: Removing a single center does not remove its offline copies, which keep showing ratings until valid_until (up to a day). If the center withdrew permission or asked for removal, the app keeps displaying its data.
attacks.evidence: "any offline copies expire at their valid_until"

attacks.claim: The blog post is a static public claim with no retraction plan. If a center is removed or the layer is rolled back, the post still says '19 avalanche centers'.
attacks.evidence: "Blog post: 'Avalanche forecasts from 19 avalanche centers across the US and Canada, now in Ridgeline Maps.'"

attacks.claim: The rollback claim 'no stale ratings remain on phones' is not supported by the QA. Purge is described as happening on next launch, but the rollback mechanism takes effect on next foreground, and a flag-off device can't be checked while offline.
attacks.evidence: "takes effect on next app foreground" / "offline forecast data purged on next launch" / "so no stale ratings remain on phones"

attacks.claim: The 3-day QA window and the 'all 19 centers' match are not tied to dates or season. Several centers may have had no forecasts, and the Nov 23 'check that all 19 centers render' is a manual step with no defined pass criterion.
attacks.evidence: "All 19 centers: all three band ratings... match the center's own site for 3 consecutive days" / "after a check that all 19 centers render"

attacks.claim: The CDN budget only alerts at $400/month with no hard cap or throttle, so runaway traffic can exceed budget unchecked.
attacks.evidence: "CDN budget alert at $400/month"

attacks.claim: The endpoint is unauthenticated and the per-IP limit is only enforced at origin. Varying the bbox bypasses CDN caching, and the rate limit is per IP, so many IPs can multiply origin load.
attacks.evidence: "rate limited at origin to 120 req/min per IP (CDN-cached responses are not counted)"

attacks.claim: WADE is the sole data source and the CDN vendor is unnamed. Exit cost and fallback if WADE terms change are not addressed.
attacks.evidence: "using forecasts published by the regional avalanche centers in the Western Avalanche Data Exchange (WADE)" / ABSENT: fallback or exit plan

attacks.claim: Center removal is a config edit with no described test or automated check that the removal propagated to offline copies.
attacks.evidence: "A single center can be removed by editing config/avy_centers.json"

attacks.claim: The 26 h per-center staleness alert is longer than a typical 24 h valid_until window, so the alert fires after forecasts have already expired in the app.
attacks.evidence: "any center not updated for 26 h during its season" / "valid_until"

attacks.claim: No attack. Expired and no-forecast zones share the gray hatched fill, but their labels differ and the QA included legibility checks.
attacks.evidence: "Forecast expired [time]" / "No current forecast"

attacks.claim: No attack. The layer delivers the stated use case; the request to show ratings to backcountry users is consistent with the source agreement.
attacks.evidence: "Tapping a zone opens a summary card and a link to the center's full forecast."

attacks.claim: No attack. The layer toggle and card are a single tap and no extra steps are added.
attacks.evidence: "Layer toggle: Map layers > Avalanche forecast."

attacks.claim: No attack. Color-blind simulations, VoiceOver/TalkBack, and 200% text were tested with labels that carry the level.
attacks.evidence: "levels distinguishable via label text"
